text:
marco: quick take needed. proposing an activation-fence model that uses a monotonic activation_seq in the manifest. operator must atomically move from applied->fenced->activated. goal: make partial-apply detection trivial and enable safe GC of old seeds. thoughts?

olivia: activation_seq sounds good. important to define how fencing is verifiable offline. we should include a signed fence blob that contains activation_seq, manifest_hash, and operator_id. offline installers can provide that blob from an HSM-backed signer.

devon: to prevent split-brain we should require a short-lived lease for the activation phase. operator obtains lease, writes local apply state, creates a "fence request" in the CRD, waits for signer confirmation, then flips activated. if lease lost, operator must abort and surface as ERROR.

tanya: related: GC policy. we can't keep every seed/model on disk. propose default: retain last 2 activation_seq versions per component, tombstone others after 72h. tombstone must be reversible until final GC window. that helps operators rollback quickly while bounding disk.

liam: implementation detail: store per-chunk content-addressed blocks in a small blobstore (/var/lib/redwood/modelstore). maintain a refcount map keyed by block-hash. when applying a bundle, increment refs for blocks used; on tombstone decrement and schedule GC. GC pass should be rate-limited and crashesafe.

kevin: +1 on content-addressing. also recommend using blake3 with a short canonical prefix for keys. consider a compact bloom filter per-bundle to speed preflight dedupe checks when streaming multiple bundles.

ruth: operator UX: we need explicit operator states: PendingFetch, Fetched, Applied, Fenced, Activating, Activated, Failed. UI should show last-successful-activated-seq and available rollbacks. also add 'preview' mode to show expected block fetch size before starting.

ops-bot: note: runbook stub created for partial-apply recovery. see /runbooks/activation-fence-recovery.md (draft).

marco: what about physical seed transfer (USB)? streaming is impossible there; we need a signed manifest + chunk map and a deterministic apply plan that operator can verify without outside network.

olivia: for USB: we produce an "offline bundle" format: manifest.json, chunk-index.bin, payload.tar.zst shards (content addressed). manifest contains activation_seq and a signer_chain array. operator verifies chain using local KMS public keys, validates chunk checksums, then proceeds to Apply. final activation requires either HSM-signed fence (if available) or operator confirmation (manual).

devon: corner case: power loss during fencing. operator must record a fenced marker file with activation_seq+lease_id; on restart it reconciles: if lease expired -> operator pauses and requires manual un-fence or re-obtain signer. if lease still valid -> complete activation. this avoids double-activation.

tanya: monitoring/telemetry: emit metrics for fetch_bytes_total, chunks_fetched, resume_tokens_issued, activation_latency_seconds, gc_bytes_reclaimed. add structured logs for apply steps with component & activation_seq.

liam: testing: we need a failure harness that injects mid-apply powercut, corrupted chunk, slow signer, signer unavailable, and resume-token expiry. replicate across k8s using a chaos-job.

kevin: security: offline signer keys must be abstracted via a signer-plugin interface so customers can plug HSM, KMS, or a manual signer. signer-plugin API: sign(manifest)->signed_fence, verify(manifest,signed_fence)->bool. provide a reference sidecar that uses local KMS table.

marco: sketch config for operator CRD (proto-ish):
```yaml
spec:
  applyWindowSeconds: 1800
  resumeTokenTTLSeconds: 86400
  gc:
    retainVersions: 2
    tombstoneDelaySeconds: 259200
status:
  components:
    - name: model-a
      applyState: Fetched
      activationSeq: "42"
      resumeTokenHash: "b3af..."
      fetchOffset: "0"
  leaderLease:
    owner: operator-1
    expiresAt: 2027-01-01T12:00:00Z
```

ruth: also include a feature-flag to enable canary-apply where we fence+activate only a single replica first, wait health-check window, then roll to full. useful for large model changes.

ops-bot: reminder: make sure runbook includes steps to inspect /var/log/redwood/apply.log and modelstore/refcounts.db.

marco: next actions: 1) I'll update RFC to include activation_seq, fence blob structure, and offline bundle layout; 2) tanya & liam to draft GC/refcount design; 3) kevin to draft signer-plugin API + reference sidecar; 4) devon to write chaos harness for resume/powercut tests; 5) ruth to mock operator UI states and preview UX. will ping once branch is up.

olivia: minor note: ensure manifest evolution supports "component renames" and stable ids so refcounts stay correct across renames.

marco: good catch. include stable component_id GUIDs in manifest schema. thanks all :rocket:
